review.body: { use crate :: burn :: { CandidateRule , Encoding } ; let crate :: burn :: PolicyInput { identity , edition , sequence , initial_marker , placement_procedure , cadence , verification_profile , published_at , genesis_at , stability_buffer , open_placement , encoding , candidate_rule , } = input ; let mut digest = Sha256 :: new () ; digest . update (MARKER_POLICY_RECIPE . as_bytes ()) ; digest . update ([0]) ; for text in [identity , edition , sequence , initial_marker , placement_procedure , cadence , verification_profile ,] { digest . update ((text . len () as u64) . to_be_bytes ()) ; digest . update (text . as_bytes ()) ; } for value in [published_at , genesis_at , stability_buffer] { digest . update (value . to_be_bytes ()) ; } digest . update ([u8 :: from (* open_placement)]) ; digest . update ([match encoding { Encoding :: CompleteList => 0 , Encoding :: PublicCommitment => 1 , Encoding :: WholePrefixAcceptAll => 2 , }]) ; digest . update ([match candidate_rule { CandidateRule :: FirstValidInHistoryOrder => 0 , CandidateRule :: UniquePerIndex => 1 , }]) ; digest . finalize () . into () }
review.item_premise: This body hashes every public policy field with explicit versioned framing. Its digest is an internal content commitment, not a protocol serialization or secret. Trace records the public input and computed bytes. The policy declaration carries its recipe identifier and digest; binding compares both after validation, and the digest exhaustively destructures all policy fields without changing v1 framing. The one recipe constant supplies the framed domain and binder comparison; unsupported recipes refuse separately before content comparison. The raw digest helper remains recomputation rather than publication.
